reason: Re-opened the packet for Katha 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 (Sitarama Sastri 1928). Śaṅkara on 1.2.2: ‘both the sweet and the good become as it were mingled, and approach man. Therefore the intelligent man examines both the sweet and the good as a flamingo separates milk and water … divides them both and follows the good alone’. ‘Arriving as if mingled’ keeps his qualifier, and ‘parting them as a flamingo parts milk from water’ is his image, so the reading carries without drift and the locator is right. Plain sense against day.js: Yama opens the teaching at 1.2.1 (‘These two, having different ends, bind a man’) after Nachiketas has refused sons, wealth, long life and the maidens (1.1.23 to 29, and 1.2.3 ‘Thou hast not accepted this garland’). ‘Every person’ generalises ‘a man’ slightly, in the direction of Śaṅkara’s ‘all men’, but stays within the generic sense of the text; not landed. One commentator, school not required; no comparison; tone fine. verse.js ok (1.2.2, at [48]); entry-check ok.
better: Optional tightening of the plain sense to the text’s own terms: ‘two aims that bind a person’ in place of ‘two aims that bind every person’.
